source_text: fær; nom. acc: gen. færes; dat. fære; pl. nom. acc. faru; gen. fara; dat. farum, n: fær; gen. dat. acc. fære; pl. nom. gen. acc. fara; dat. farum; f? [from faran to go]. I. a going, journey, way, journeying, expedition; &i-short;ter, exp&e-short;d&i-long;tio bell&i-short;ca :-- Ánes dæges fær &i-short;ter diei, Lk. Bos. 2, 44. Gódige folces fær facilitate the people's journeying, L. Pen. 15; Th. ii. 282, 9. Ðæt wæs fær micel that was a great expedition, Invent. Crs. Recd. 1295; El. 646. II. that in which a journey or voyage is made,-a vehicle, vessel, ship; veh&i-short;c&u-short;lum, n&a-long;vis :-- Ðú ðær [Th. Grn. ðæt that] fær gewyrc make thou that vessel, Cd. 65; Th. 79, 6; Gen. 1307. Fær Noes Noah's ark, Cd. 66; Th. 80, 4; Gen. 1323. [Piers P.
